title: Telling an Anecdote: Close Calls & Second Attempts

sections.content: You know *estar a punto de* + infinitive from B1 Unit 1 (in the *imperfecto* for an interrupted moment: *estaba a punto de salir cuando sonó el teléfono*) and *volver a* + infinitive from A2 Unit 28 and B2 Unit 23. In lively spoken anecdotes, two sharper uses stand out. First, *estar a punto de* in the **preterite** (*estuve a punto de rendirme*, *estuvimos a punto de cancelar la cena*) narrates a close call that was narrowly avoided (*por los pelos*). Second, *volver a* + infinitive pairs with *no* for emphatic vows after a mishap (*¡No vuelvo a improvisar una receta diez minutos antes!*) and with object pronouns either before *volver* or attached to the infinitive (*la volvió a probar* / *volvió a probarla*).

sections.title: Close calls and vows in everyday storytelling
rows: Interrupted scene (*Estaba a punto de sacar la bandeja cuando sonó el timbre.*).
Close call narrowly avoided (*Estuve a punto de cancelar la cena, pero nos salvamos por los pelos.*).
*Volvió a medir el condimento al instante.*
*No vuelvo a cocinar sin leer la receta entera.* ('I'm never doing that again.').

items.spanish: Estuvimos a punto de cancelar la cena, pero Carlos nos sacó de un apuro por los pelos.
items.english: We were on the verge of cancelling dinner, but Carlos got us out of a jam by the skin of our teeth.

items.spanish: Cuando todo parecía salir mal, volvió a probar el guiso y encontró la falla al instante.
items.english: When everything seemed to be going wrong, she tasted the stew again and found the flaw instantly.

items.spanish: ¡No vuelvo a improvisar un postre cinco minutos antes de que lleguen los invitados!
items.english: I am never improvising a dessert five minutes before the guests arrive again!

items.spanish: Al final la cena salió redonda y logramos salvar la noche.
items.english: In the end dinner turned out brilliantly and we managed to save the evening.

sections.content: Never drop the preposition *de* in *estar a punto de* or *a* in *volver a* (*Estuve a punto cancelar* and *Volvió probarlo* are both wrong). In lively speech, the present tense *¡No vuelvo a…!* works as a strong future vow ('I'm never … again!').
